text:
jamal: @here Dedicated pool d-pool-west showing sustained latency spike and throughput drop, started ~14:02 UTC. p50 ~130ms -> 600ms, p95/p99 spiking to 1.4s+. Customers reporting SLA violations. Investigating.
priya: on it. any recent deploys or config changes?
jamal: deploy-bot: rollout prod/dedicated/d-pool-west completed 13:58 UTC (no user-config changes).
alex: looking at node-level metrics now. GPU util on some hosts at 98%, others idling. weird placement pattern.
sasha: I see a sudden increase in KV cache miss rate for sessions served by that pool — from 7% -> 48% around 14:01.
ben: batching traces show larger-than-usual batches forming then stalling on a few requests. batcher metrics: batch_size_mean jumped from 12 -> 38, batch_latency_p95 from 20ms -> 550ms.
priya: could be noisy neighbor — a tenant with long beam/ASR jobs eating VRAM and forcing context swapping. Alex, can you confirm per-GPU process list?
alex: yes: on host gpu-17 one container (tenant: corp-8) running beam-search job with persistent allocations, memory pinned ~100%. Other model workers moved to GPU 15/16 causing fragmentation.
jamal: pushing a quick mitigation: draining corp-8 and evicting non-critical jobs from gpu-17. Will scale out if necessary.
priya: also noticed kernel-selection logs around 14:00: some layers fell back from optimized path fast_attention_v2 -> scalar_attention_fallback due to unexpected sequence length 8192 vs usual 2048. That fallback increased per-token time ~4x in trace.
sasha: snippet from runtime profiler:
```
[14:00:57] kernel_selector: chosen=fast_attention_v2(shape=2048) fallback=scalar_attention_fallback(shape=8192) reason=seq_len_mismatch
[14:01:01] exec_time: fast_attention_v2: 2.3ms/token, scalar_attention_fallback: 9.8ms/token
```
ben: batching heuristic also hit the "max_batch_delay_ms" bump because some requests had large seq_len and blocked flush. Our continuous-batching algorithm waits up to 80ms for stragglers; that plus fallback kernels compounded latency.
alex: placement issue: scheduler pinned a warm model instance to gpu-17 because of affinity tag, while corp-8 tenant got auto-scaled there due to quota misconfig. Looks like quota for corp-8 had an unusually high burst allowance (quota config 500 -> 5k tokens/min) applied by mistake at 13:57.
jamal: can we confirm when quota change landed? deploy-bot, any config updates?
deploy-bot: config-change: quotas.yaml updated by infra-ci at 13:56 UTC (PR#8342). Change: corp-8 burst_quota: 500 -> 5000 (intended for corp-8-staging but labeled prod).
priya: that explains noisy neighbor. corp-8 surged and pinned GPUs, causing other workers to be pushed to suboptimal hosts and forcing kernel fallbacks and KV cold misses.
sasha: also saw KV cache eviction logs: several sessions evicted due to memory pressure, TTL purge triggered incorrectly because of a bug in session key normalization. entries evicted ~14:00-14:05 causing cold-cache regen cost.
ben: profiling summary attached in logs:
```
14:00-14:10 summary:
- GPU saturation on 3/12 hosts
- avg kernel exec time up 3.6x on attention layers
- cache miss rate +41%
- mean batch size up 220%
- tail latency increase correlates with corp-8 spikes
```
alex: mitigation steps executed: 14:08 drained corp-8 from gpu-17, scaled dedicated pool +2 nodes at 14:12, reverted quotas.yaml PR at 14:17, resumed normal placement policies 14:20.
jamal: monitoring — p95 down to ~180ms and p99 trending toward normal. SLA still at risk; we'll keep this open until 2 hours stable.
priya: action items:
- revert PR authoring flow to add env tag check (assigned: alex)
- add quota change preflight to infra CI (assigned: ben)
- fix KV session normalization bug (assigned: sasha)
- add metric alert for kernel-fallback rate > 1% (assigned: jamal)

ben: logging note: add correlation id in placement decisions to trace tenant->GPU mapping.
jamal: for postmortem, timeline + root cause: incorrect quota PR caused noisy neighbor -> GPU placement fragmentation + KV evictions + kernel fallback due to longer seq_len -> combined effect produced latency spikes and SLA breach window.
priya: tagging support and customer success to notify affected customers, datadog dashboard updated with annotations.
jamal: closing updates: last degraded spike 14:32 UTC, system stable 14:28-14:40 trending good. Keeping incident open for 2h monitoring.
ben: :thumbsup: good job team. will draft postmortem after root-cause fixes landed.
priya: thanks everyone, switching to follow-up channel for postmortem notes.
oncall-bot: Incident INCIDENT-2026-1087 updated: status=mitigated, severity=sev2, owners=[jamal,priya,alex,ben,sasha]."
